passages.text: If any of you has a grievance against another, how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses Christians.
He asks about disputes among believers.
If one of you has a complaint against another believer, do not go to secular courts.
Do not seek judgment from those who do not follow God.
Instead, bring your case before the saints.
Let the church judge between believers.
passages.original: Τολμᾷ τις ὑμῶν πρᾶγμα ἔχων πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κρίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῶν ἀδίκων καὶ οὐχὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων

passages.text: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?
passages.sermon:
The saints are God's holy people.
The saints will judge the world.
You are part of the saints.
You will judge the world.
You must know this.
If you will judge the world, you can judge small matters.
You are able to decide even the least important cases among you.
passages.original: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἅγιοι τὸν κόσμον κρινοῦσιν καὶ εἰ ἐν ὑμῖν κρίνεται ὁ κόσμος ἀνάξιοί ἐστε κριτηρίων ἐλαχίστων

passages.text: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!
passages.sermon:
We are Christians.
We will judge angels.
We have great authority from God.
We will judge even heavenly beings.
We can certainly judge matters of this life.
We are able to handle everyday disputes.
passages.original: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἀγγέλους κρινοῦμεν μήτιγε βιωτικά

passages.text: So if you need to settle everyday matters, do you appoint as judges those of no standing in the church?
passages.sermon:
You are Christians.
You sometimes have disputes about everyday matters.
You need to settle these disputes.
You choose judges for these matters.
You appoint people who have no standing in the church as judges.
These people are not respected in the church.
You let them decide your everyday cases.
passages.original: Βιωτικὰ μὲν οὖν κριτήρια ἐὰν ἔχητε τοὺς ἐξουθενημένους ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τούτους καθίζετε

passages.text: I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul feels shame for the church.
Paul says, "I say this to your shame."
Paul asks a question.
Paul asks if there is anyone wise among them.
Paul asks if anyone can judge between his brothers.
Paul expects someone in the church to be wise.
Paul expects someone to settle disputes between believers.
passages.original: πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λέγω οὕτως οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφὸς ὃς δυνήσεται διακρῖναι ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses Christians who are brothers in faith.
One Christian takes another Christian to court.
They do this before unbelievers.
They let non-Christians judge their disputes.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀδελφὸς μετὰ ἀδελφοῦ κρίνεται καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ ἀπίστων

passages.text: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christians in Corinth.
You have lawsuits among yourselves.
This means you are already completely defeated.
Why do you not rather accept being wronged?
Why do you not rather accept being cheated?
passages.original: ἤδη μὲν οὖν ὅλως ἥττημα ὑμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι κρίματα ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθε διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀποστερεῖσθε

passages.text: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!
passages.sermon: You cheat others.\r\nYou do wrong to others.\r\nYou do these things to your own brothers.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς ἀδικεῖτε καὶ ἀποστερεῖτε καὶ τοῦτο ἀδελφούς

passages.text: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
The wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Do not be deceived.
Sexually immoral people will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Idolaters will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Adulterers will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Men who submit to or perform homosexual acts will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Thieves will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Greedy people will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Drunkards will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Verbal abusers will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Swindlers will not inherit the kingdom of God.
passages.original: Ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἄδικοι Θεοῦ βασιλείαν οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν μὴ πλανᾶσθε οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε εἰδωλολάτραι οὔτε μοιχοὶ οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται οὔτε κλέπται οὔτε πλεονέκται οὐ μέθυσοι οὐ λοίδοροι οὐχ ἅρπαγες βασιλείαν Θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν

passages.text: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
passages.sermon:
Some of you once lived in these sinful ways.
You did wrong things in the past.
But now God has changed you.
God has washed you clean.
God has made you holy.
God has made you right with Him.
He did this through the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
He did this by the Spirit of our God.
passages.original: καὶ ταῦτά τινες ἦτε ἀλλὰ ἀπελούσασθε ἀλλὰ ἡγιάσθητε ἀλλὰ ἐδικαιώθητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν

passages.text: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
Paul says, “Everything is permissible for me.”
But not everything is beneficial.
Paul repeats, “Everything is permissible for me.”
But I will not be mastered by anything.
passages.original: Πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει Πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγὼ ἐξουσιασθήσομαι ὑπό τινος

passages.text: “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
passages.sermon:
God created food for the stomach.
God created the stomach for food.
God will destroy both food and the stomach.
God did not create the body for sexual immorality.
God created the body for the Lord.
The Lord cares for the body.
passages.original: Τὰ βρώματα τῇ κοιλίᾳ καὶ ἡ κοιλία τοῖς βρώμασιν ὁ δὲ Θεὸς καὶ ταύτην καὶ ταῦτα καταργήσει τὸ δὲ σῶμα οὐ τῇ πορνείᾳ ἀλλὰ τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ ὁ Κύριος τῷ σώματι

passages.text: By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.
passages.sermon: God is powerful.\r\nGod used His power to raise the Lord Jesus from the dead.\r\nGod will also use His power to raise us from the dead.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς καὶ τὸν Κύριον ἤγειρεν καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξεγερεῖ διὰ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!
passages.sermon:
Your bodies belong to Christ.
Your bodies are members of Christ.
I must not join the members of Christ to a prostitute.
I must never do this.
passages.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν μέλη Χριστοῦ ἐστιν ἄρας οὖν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιήσω πόρνης μέλη μὴ γένοιτο

passages.text: Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”
passages.sermon: A man who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her.\r\nScripture says, “The two will become one flesh.”
passages.original: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ὁ κολλώμενος τῇ πόρνῃ ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν Ἔσονται γάρ φησίν Οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν

passages.text: But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is Jesus Christ.
Anyone who joins himself to the Lord becomes one with Him.
This unity is spiritual.
He who unites with the Lord is one spirit with Him.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος τῷ Κυρίῳ ἓν πνεῦμά ἐστιν

passages.text: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul teaches the church in Corinth.
\r\nPaul warns about sexual immorality.
\r\nFlee from sexual immorality.
\r\nEvery other sin a person commits is outside the body.
\r\nBut sexual sin is different.
\r\nThe person who sins sexually sins against his own body.
passages.original: Φεύγετε τὴν πορνείαν πᾶν ἁμάρτημα ὃ ἐὰν ποιήσῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ δὲ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει

passages.text: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.
passages.sermon:
Your body is a temple.
The Holy Spirit lives in you.
God gave you the Holy Spirit.
You do not belong to yourself.
God bought you at a price.
Glorify God with your body.
passages.original: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν Ἁγίου Πνεύματός ἐστιν οὗ ἔχετε ἀπὸ Θεοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἑαυτῶν ἠγοράσθητε γὰρ τιμῆς δοξάσατε δὴ τὸν Θεὸν ἐν τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν
